quote: But what set humanity firmly on the path of Science was noticing that certain modes of thinking uncovered beliefs that let us manipulate the world.
content: Mokyr is cited here against a thesis Mokyr argues for. The central claim of The Gifts of Athena is that sustained growth began when propositional knowledge and prescriptive technique were coupled into a feedback loop, so that craft practice could be explained, generalized and improved rather than merely copied — which is the essay’s "noticing that certain modes of thinking uncovered beliefs that let us manipulate the world," stated as economic history. That craft preceded theory in the first instance is not in dispute and is not what the essay denies; the steam engine gave thermodynamics its subject matter, and thermodynamics then gave engineering the efficiency limits that craft could not find by trial. The Baconian story the annotation calls a myth is the one Mokyr reconstructs with evidence.

quote: it has a special and admirable purity
content: The essay names this failing itself, in the same passage: curiosity "is not sufficient," it does not stay to verify, and that is the stated reason pragmatism and morality are introduced alongside it. Loewenstein’s gap theory is in fact congenial to the essay’s claim of purity in the sense meant, namely that the drive is indifferent to whether the answer is welcome; a motive that pursues nearly-closed gaps regardless of what lies in them is not one that flinches from unpleasant truths. The tilt toward the easy is a claim about the agenda curiosity sets, not about whether curiosity distorts the answers, and only the second would bear on the essay’s argument.
